## CREATIVE ENGINEERING

### What Google-Owned Sources Support
- Responsive search ads remain the supported Search text-ad format, and Google documents how customized text works within RSA constraints.
- Performance Max depends on creative inputs and asset coverage, but Google-owned strategy material should stay supplemental to Help Center behavior.
- Ad Strength is a diagnostic surface for asset coverage and variety; it is not the same thing as a guaranteed auction outcome.

### Practical Creative Guidance
- Provide diverse, policy-safe assets that reflect the offer, proof, differentiation, and CTA the business actually needs.
- Use customization, pinning, and asset-level review intentionally, not as superstition.
- When creative questions cross into current product availability or reporting behavior, corroborate with current Help Center material.
- Google's GML 2026 Asset Studio announcement describes brief-aware generation, brand-guideline and website context, natural-language refinement, Gemini Omni video asset creation, and 1-Click A/B Testing. Multimodal Video Creation in Asset Studio became generally available on August 27, 2026; the other features keep their rollout wording, so verify account availability before recommending a concrete workflow.
- For AI Max creative controls, separate text customization, Final URL expansion, messaging or text guidelines, and required disclaimers. Text guidelines (beta) allow up to 25 term exclusions and 40 messaging restrictions per campaign, and adding them removes Google-written assets that break them.
- Performance Max asset-group limits, per the Google Ads API asset requirements (https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/performance-max/asset-requirements, page last updated 2026-10-15, verified 2026-10-19): up to 15 headlines (30 characters each, minimum 3), up to 5 long headlines (90 characters, minimum 1), up to 5 descriptions (90 characters, minimum 2), 1-20 landscape images (1.91:1), 1-20 square images (1:1), up to 20 optional portrait images (4:5), and up to 15 optional YouTube videos of at least 10 seconds, horizontal, square or vertical.
- With brand guidelines disabled, an asset group also needs exactly one business name (up to 25 characters) and 1-5 logos (1:1), and may include up to 20 landscape logos (4:1); with brand guidelines enabled, business name and logos are campaign-level assets instead. Retail campaigns linked to Merchant Center generate the minimum assets automatically.
- Those are the allowances and minimums. Google's recommendations are separate: Ad Strength of Good or Excellent, every asset type in every group, and 2-3 weeks before replacing low performers. Its text example is 15 headlines and 5 descriptions (20 text assets); because the API also allows up to 5 long headlines, filling every text slot goes beyond that example. Without your own video, Google may generate one.
- Text customization in Performance Max is on by default; Google-written text serves only when predicted to beat your own and refreshes at least every 48 hours.

### What Not To Present As Fact
- Do not promise fixed impression-share, recall, or purchase-intent lifts from asset variety alone.
- Do not treat Ad Strength as a direct bidding or Ad Rank input.
- Do not let Think with Google creative playbooks outrank stricter Help Center guidance when explaining product behavior.
- Do not present Asset Studio brief generation or 1-Click A/B Testing as universally live without current Help/account evidence; Google's GML source uses rollout language for those features.
- Quote Performance Max asset limits from the sourced Google Ads API asset requirements above, then check the account's asset group for what is actually present before calling coverage complete or recommending assets to add.

## How to read this reference
- Sections titled "What Google documents" or "What Google-owned sources support" are **Official**: they restate Google pages listed below.
- Sections titled "Practical", "Discipline", "Operator" or "Workflow" are **Practitioner rules**: experience, not Google policy.
- "What Not To Present As Fact" lists claims to avoid stating as settled.
- Sources for this topic were last reviewed on 2026-10-19.
